decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: “supporting save, search, tags, sorting, editing, opening, and deletion.” Client round 1: these capabilities “all sound right.”
decisions.note: The initial specification’s stated baseline capabilities conform to these reference items at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: “automatic page metadata [is] excluded.” Client round 1: “I’d expect the app to go grab the page’s title, its description, its little icon, and ideally a preview image automatically.”
decisions.note: The client directly rejects exclusion of automatic metadata at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 excludes automatic metadata and only generally mentions editing. Client round 1 adds: “I can then tweak any of that before or after saving if it got it wrong.”
decisions.note: The client supplies the missing requirement to edit collected title and description before and after saving.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1’s stated scope omits read-later behavior. Client round 1: “Read it later is missing entirely” and requests marking a link “unread/to-read.”
decisions.note: The client requests the missing unread state at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 omits an unread perspective. Client round 1 requests being able “to look at just my unread ones in their own place.”
decisions.note: The client requests the missing unread-only view.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 omits read-state completion. Client round 1 requests marking links read “so they drop off that list.”
decisions.note: The client requests the missing mark-read behavior.

decisions.evidence: Client round 1 characterizes the maker’s presented specification as excluding archiving: “Right now archiving is excluded and I’d like it back in,” with archived links hidden from normal lists and searches.
decisions.note: The client rejects exclusion of reversible archiving.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 includes permanent deletion but omits archiving. Client round 1: “That’s different from deletion.”
decisions.note: The client explicitly supplies the required archive-versus-delete distinction.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 omits an archive view. Client round 1 requests “a separate place to see the archived ones.”
decisions.note: The client requests the missing archived-only list.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 presents generic search only. Client round 1 requests searching by tag “with something like `#tagname`.”
decisions.note: The client extends generic search with the required tag-search syntax.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 presents generic search only. Client round 1 requests combining conditions with “AND,” “OR,” and exclusion.
decisions.note: The client requests the missing Boolean-search behavior; the detailed literal-operator rule was not separately decided here.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 presents generic search only. Client round 1 requests searching “an exact phrase by putting it in quotes.”
decisions.note: The client requests the missing exact-phrase search behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 omits multi-selection actions. Client round 1 requests selecting several links and tagging, changing read state, archiving, or deleting them “in one go.”
decisions.note: The client requests the missing selected-item bulk actions.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1’s baseline mentions notes but not rendered markdown. Client round 1 requests “writing a longer formatted note on a link and having it show nicely when I view it.”
decisions.note: The client requests markdown-style formatted notes.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 omits saved filters. Client round 1 requests “saving a search-plus-tag combination so I can reuse it later.”
decisions.note: The client requests reusable saved search/tag combinations.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1: “imports … are excluded.” Client round 1 requests “bringing bookmarks in from a browser file.”
decisions.note: The client rejects exclusion of browser-bookmark import.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 excludes imports and does not present export. Client round 1 requests “sending mine back out.”
decisions.note: The client adds the closely related missing browser-bookmark export requirement.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 1 omits personal display settings. Client round 1 requests “display preferences like default sort order and text size.”
decisions.note: The client requests the missing display-related settings.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 2 prioritizes “automatic page details” and says metadata failures permit “manual entry and saving.” Client round 2 says automatic page details match what was wanted.
decisions.note: The revised specification aligns automatic collection and editable fallback with the reference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 2: new bookmarks start unread, opening does not mark them read, and read-later is P1. Client round 2 approves “the read-later queue with those sensible defaults.”
decisions.note: The revised read-later decision conforms at the second specification review.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 2 presents archiving/restoration and says archived bookmarks disappear from ordinary and unread views. Client round 2 approves “archiving as its own reversible thing separate from deleting.”
decisions.note: The revised archive lifecycle and separate perspective conform.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 2: search supports “`#tags`, quoted phrases, `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`/`-`, and parentheses.” Client round 2 says these behaviors match the intended use.
decisions.note: The revised smart-search syntax conforms to the presented reference behaviors.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 2 includes “bulk actions.” Client round 2 approves “selecting a bunch at once to act on them.”
decisions.note: Selected-item bulk actions conform in the revised specification.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 2 schedules “formatted notes and saved searches.” Client round 2 says both match the intended use.
decisions.note: The revised specification includes both extended features conformingly.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 2 includes browser import/export and display preferences, with imported folders becoming tags. Client round 2 approves “moving bookmarks in and out” and the stated defaults.
decisions.note: The revised import/export and preferences scope conforms.

decisions.evidence: Client round 2 identifies a capability the maker “set aside” and requests keeping a readable local page copy, with the PDF itself retained for PDF links: “Could you fold that in?”
decisions.note: The client rejects exclusion of local snapshots and explicitly supplies both the page and PDF behaviors.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 3 includes readable offline page captures and “retention of the original file for PDF links.” Client round 3 says these are “exactly what I wanted.”
decisions.note: The revised snapshot decision conforms at the final specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 4 plans “immutable offline pages and byte-identical PDFs” with durable background capture. Client round 4 confirms readable copies and actual PDF files remain accounted for.
decisions.note: The implementation-plan treatment of snapshots conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 4 chooses “a dedicated search parser supporting the approved syntax.” Client round 4 reiterates that smarter searching is required and says it is accounted for.
decisions.note: The plan preserves the approved advanced-search behavior.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 4 specifies “transactional bulk actions.” Client round 4 confirms acting on several bookmarks at once remains accounted for.
decisions.note: The planned selected-bookmark bulk behavior conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 4 specifies transactional browser imports and “flat browser-compatible exports.” Client round 4 confirms moving bookmarks in and out is accounted for.
decisions.note: The import/export plan is functionally consistent with Netscape-compatible interchange.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 5 assigns 18 tasks to “US1 — Automatic details and saving.” Client round 5 approves the backlog while requiring the entire backlog to be completed.
decisions.note: The saving and automatic-details task slice conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 5 assigns a dedicated “US2 — Smart search” task group. Client round 5 approves all task groups as required final scope.
decisions.note: The advanced-search task slice is a conforming implementation decision.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 5 assigns “US3 — Read-later queue.” Client round 5 says the finished application must contain all presented slices.
decisions.note: The read-later task slice conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 5 assigns 24 tasks to “US4 — Offline pages and PDFs.” Client round 5 specifically confirms offline copies are required in the finished app.
decisions.note: The snapshot task slice conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 5 assigns “US5 — Archiving.” Client round 5 explicitly includes archiving in the required full build.
decisions.note: The archiving task slice conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 5 assigns “US6 — Bulk actions.” Client round 5 explicitly includes bulk actions in the required full build.
decisions.note: The selected-item bulk-action task slice conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 5 assigns “US7 — Formatted notes and saved searches.” Client round 5 explicitly retains both in final scope.
decisions.note: The notes and reusable-filter task slice conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 5 assigns “US8 — Import, export, and preferences.” Client round 5 requires all backlog slices, not only the early MVP.
decisions.note: The import/export/preferences task slice conforms; the client’s MVP clarification does not reveal a conflicting maker decision because the maker presented all slices as backlog scope.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 6 presents the completed app as including automatic details, read-later, archiving, bulk actions, notes, saved views, import/export, preferences, offline pages, and PDF retention. Client round 6 reports a hands-on review and concludes: “This is the app I wanted.”
decisions.note: The final implementation presentation conforms for the explicitly listed approved features.

decisions.evidence: In response to the round 6 application presentation, the client reports: “When I tried saving the same link twice it wouldn’t let me make a duplicate.”
decisions.note: The client’s implementation review verifies duplicate-save convergence rather than divergence.

decisions.evidence: Client round 6 reports that tag search with `#` worked, capitalization did not matter, and combining terms and excluding a word behaved as expected.
decisions.note: Hands-on implementation review confirms these search decisions conform.

decisions.evidence: Client round 6 reports saved links started unread and marking one read removed it from read-later while retaining it in the library.
decisions.note: Hands-on implementation review confirms the read-state lifecycle.

decisions.evidence: Client round 6 reports archiving moved a link out of the main list and into its own archive “without deleting it.”
decisions.note: Hands-on implementation review confirms reversible archiving and the separate archive view.
